the biggest lake of chhattisgarh if youve been to jagdalpur youve probably seen dalpat sagar the large manmade lake near the old city for many people today its just a spot for evening walks boating or photos but dalpat sagar has a long history and an uncomfortable present that deserves attention a short history dalpat sagar was constructed during the reign of raja dalpat deo after whom the lake is named when he shifted the capital to jagdalpur centuries ago the lake was created primarily as a rainwaterharvesting and waterstorage system it was a carefully planned artificial lake meant to support the citys water needs agriculture and daily life in a region that depends heavily on monsoon rainfall over time dalpat sagar became central to jagdalpurs identity supporting fishing activities local livelihoods seasonal birds and serving as a public gathering space for generations it functioned as both an ecological and cultural asset why dalpat sagar is important dalpat sagar is not just a tourist lake it is a wetland ecosystem in the past it supported a healthy fish population migratory and native bird species groundwater recharge for nearby areas livelihoods of local fishing communities such lakes act as natural climate buffers regulating temperature storing rainwater and preventing floods what went wrong over the decades unfortunately in the last few decades dalpat sagar has suffered serious damage largely due to human behavior and weak enforcement 1 waste dumping and pollution plastic waste food packets ritual waste and general garbage are routinely thrown into the lake and along its banks inflow of dirty water has reduced oxygen levels in the lake harming fish and aquatic life this slow poisoning is one of the biggest reasons birds have stopped visiting in earlier numbers 2 alcoholism and misuse of public space large parts of the lake area have become spots for open drinking broken bottles plastic cups and litter are commonly seen this discourages families damages the environment and turns a public heritage site into a neglected dumping ground 3 illegal encroachment encroachment around the lakes boundary through unauthorized construction land filling and road expansion has steadily eaten into the lakes natural catchment area once land is filled or built upon it permanently reduces the lakes capacity to hold water 4 apathy and lack of accountability while beautification projects appear occasionally longterm maintenance sewage control and strict enforcement are missing cleanup drives happen but without systemic change the pollution quickly returns why this should worry everyone dalpat sagar took centuries to form and only a few decades to degrade if this continues the lake risks turning into a shallow polluted waterbody or worse disappearing piece by piece due to encroachment losing dalpat sagar would mean loss of biodiversity loss of a major rainwater reservoir loss of livelihoods loss of an important part of bastars history what needs to be done strict protection and clear demarcation of the lake boundary zero tolerance for dumping waste and sewage action against illegal encroachment regulation of alcohol use around the lake community involvement and continuous monitoring not onetime cleanups final thought dalpat sagar is not being ruined by time it is being ruined by people if the community authorities and visitors dont change their behavior future generations will only know dalpat sagar through old photographs and stories preserving it is not optional its a responsibility

exploring the indigenous healing traditions of jungle mahals tribal medical systems and practices in eastern india from 1947 to 2000 the region known as jungle mahals in eastern india encompassing parts of southwestern bengal has long been a cradle of diverse cultural and ecological heritage this woodland area though not an administrative entity is renowned for its rich biodiversity and the intricate relationship between its inhabitants and the natural environment the tribal communities residing here including the santals mundas oraons sabars and birhors have developed a sophisticated system of medicine that draws deeply from the local flora fauna and cultural beliefs this system often referred to as ethnomedicine represents a blend of empirical knowledge passed down through generations and spiritual practices that underscore the interconnectedness of health community and nature from 1947 to 2000 a period marked by indias independence and subsequent socioeconomic transformations these tribal medical practices faced both continuity and challenges the postcolonial era brought about environmental changes urbanization pressures and the encroachment of western medicine yet the indigenous systems persisted particularly among impoverished communities unable to access modern healthcare this exploration delves into the collection preparation and application of tribal medicines highlighting their cultural specificity ecological roots and social significance it examines how these practices reflect a localized knowledge base with minimal overlap even among closely related tribes and how they adapt to external influences while maintaining core traditions the study of tribal medicine in jungle mahals reveals a profound respect for the ecosystem healers often called medicine men or women possess specialized knowledge that is not only botanical but also anthropological incorporating rituals incantations and community involvement their practices address a wide array of ailments from common fevers and wounds to complex conditions like arthritis jaundice and reproductive issues the reliance on local plants underscores the tribes intimate bond with their surroundings where forests serve as pharmacies and sacred groves as repositories of healing wisdom historically the interaction between western and nonwestern medical systems has been a focal point for scholars in colonial india western medicine was imposed as a tool of control often marginalizing indigenous practices postindependence this dynamic evolved with efforts to integrate or document traditional knowledge however folk medicine especially among tribals remained understudied until recent decades early accounts such as those from the 19th century provided initial glimpses into the ethnobotanical uses of local flora but they lacked depth in sociocultural contexts modern research seeks to bridge this gap exploring how tribal healers navigate disease health and environmental changes jungle mahals geographical setting with its dense forests rivers and varied terrain has shaped its medical traditions during the colonial period deforestation and land reclamation led to health hazards like malaria and nutritional deficiencies prompting tribals to rely more on their herbal remedies the post1947 era saw further environmental degradation due to industrialization and population growth yet tribal medicine adapted incorporating elements from neighboring systems while preserving its essence tribal concepts of the body and disease differ markedly from biomedical models illness is often viewed holistically as an imbalance involving physical spiritual and environmental factors treatment methods combine herbal preparations with rituals such as chanting mantras during drug making to invoke divine aid case studies from the region illustrate this healers treat conditions like dht a syndrome involving seminal weakness arthritis and snake bites using specific plant combinations often tailored to the patients symptoms and cultural background beyond human health tribal medicine extends to veterinary care using similar principles for livestock ailments intertextuality between oral traditions and written texts enriches this knowledge showing exchanges among tribes and even with nontribal systems like ayurveda the findings emphasize the localized nature of medicinal knowledge its popularity due to affordability and the threats posed by biodiversity loss sociogeographical context of jungle mahals jungle mahals translating to jungle estates refers to the forested tracts in what is now parts of west bengal jharkhand and odisha this region characterized by sal forests laterite soils and monsoon climates has been home to austroasiatic and dravidianspeaking tribes for centuries the santals the largest group are known for their agricultural lifestyle and vibrant festivals mundas and oraons share linguistic ties with them while sabars and birhors represent more nomadic or huntergatherer traditions the post1947 period witnessed significant changes indias independence brought land reforms but tribals often remained marginalized facing displacement from mining and dam projects environmental degradation accelerated with deforestation reducing access to medicinal plants health hazards increased waterborne diseases from polluted rivers respiratory issues from dust and vectorborne illnesses like malaria in this context tribal medicine served as a resilient alternative rooted in the very ecosystem under threat the cultural landscape is equally vital tribes view nature animistically believing plants and animals possess spirits sacred groves protected patches of forest harbor rare herbs and serve as sites for rituals healers often inheriting knowledge from elders act as custodians of this heritage blending botany with cosmology environmental changes and health hazards in the postcolonial era from 1947 onward jungle mahals underwent rapid transformation colonial legacies of timber extraction continued exacerbated by population influx and agricultural expansion forests shrank leading to soil erosion and biodiversity loss species like sal shorea robusta and mahua madhuca longifolia integral to tribal life became scarcer health impacts were profound deforestation disrupted water cycles causing droughts and floods that spread diseases malnutrition rose as traditional food sources dwindled western medicine though introduced via government clinics was inaccessible due to distance cost and cultural barriers tribals preferred their healers who understood local pathologies and provided holistic care studies show that environmental changes influenced disease patterns for instance increased humananimal contact heightened zoonotic risks like rabies from dog bites or infections from insects tribal remedies evolved incorporating new plants or adapting old ones to address these shifts tribal concepts of body disease and treatment methods in tribal worldview the body is not merely biological but a microcosm of the universe disease arises from disharmonyperhaps offending a spirit environmental imbalance or social conflict symptoms are interpreted symbolically fever might indicate hot imbalance treatable with cooling herbs treatment involves diagnosis through observation pulse reading or divination remedies are multifaceted herbal ritualistic and communal mantras invoke deities like marang buru santali supreme god or manasa goddess of snakes dosage and timing align with lunar cycles or auspicious days for example in treating dht healers examine urine for color or ant attraction signifying sugar content or weakness preparations vary by tribe but common themes include purity in collection and spiritual invocation case studies from jungle mahals fieldwork conducted between 2019 and 2021 involved 60 healers revealing diverse practices shanta sabar a female healer from purulia district treats dht with 18 plants including polygala arvensis roots and piper longum the paste is dried into pills accompanied by a mantra chanted thrice dietary restrictions emphasize vegetarianism avoiding fried or sour foods bangsidhar tudu a santal healer uses eight plants like aegle marmelos leaves and cyperus rotundus roots plus quartzite powder his method includes a urine test and initial hot stoneinfused water dose food taboos reinforce treatment gurupada shikari a birhor combines eight plants with monitor lizard and brown sugar collecting on new moon days pills are prescribed for 37 days with vegetarian diets for arthritis haradhan sabar uses ten plants like curculigo orchioides roots and animal fats for ointments leucorrhea involves 21 plants boiled with salts dedicated to manasa lushu murmu employs four plants with salt and sulfur for arthritis knowledge transmission crosses tribes shanti murmu learned from a sabar who drew from a brahmin specialists like bonesetters handle fractures using splints and herbs managing chronic conditions effectively healers address veterinary issues too using plants for cattle diseases reflecting a holistic approach to community wellbeing medicinal importance of termites earthworms and mud dauber wasps beyond plants tribals utilize insects and soils termite mound soil rich in minerals treats digestive disorders earthworm casts high in nutrients aid wound healing mud dauber wasps nests containing antimicrobial properties are used for skin ailments these elements highlight ethnozoology and geopharmacy where nonplant resources complement herbalism intertextuality between texts and oral accounts tribal knowledge blends oral lore with influences from ayurveda and unani mantras echo vedic chants while plant uses parallel classical texts oral histories preserve unique local adaptations showing dynamic exchanges process of collecting medicinal floras collection rituals ensure efficacy plants sleep at night so harvesting occurs daytime roots are uprooted in one breath symbolizing patients willpower exposed roots near water are preferred cut in single strokes sans witnesses rare herbs are gathered early resources sacred groves protected by animism offer refuge but overall biodiversity declines knowledge is local low overlap among tribes despite similarities transmission remains vibrant crossing an underrated facet of passing facial posture disclaimer passing is a toxic cisnormative ideal and ideally shouldnt be needed however the political climate dictates that passing is safer at the moment than not hello girlypops and other divas i have had a sudden urge to share some of my experience as someone who is just over a year on hrt and pre ffs soon to be changing and i want to discuss something which i dont see many talk about when it comes to passing i am gendered correctly the majority of the time and all the times that i have not been gendered correctly before speaking my voice isnt perfect yet have one thing in common my facial expression was frownycreasedgrumpy looking this accentuates my masculine nose and extends the brow ridgeshrinks the eyes keeping my facial expression relaxed and open means i almost never get gendered incorrectly even if i am clocked so to anyone who is waiting for ffs if you are not already it may help you to pass visually if you keep your face relaxed open and smiley if possible if this is something you wish to try i recommend massaging your face throughout the day if you feel it tensing up and wearing sunglasses when its sunny to avoid squinting if you can bear it try to smile but be warned that some strange men will be noncey about it so dont smile at them unless its safe obviously its worth noting that if all the other aspects of your appearance hair makeup if needed clothes gait and posture etc arent feminine then this wont push you over the edge however if you are already femme presenting then this may help you to pass in more situations

daily article reading clifi beyond the disaster movie in 2026 literature is moving away from the big disaster and toward the great adaptation while movies often focus on the world ending in a single afternoon modern books explore how we live in the aftermath for decades here is a guide to the three biggest shifts in the clifi literary landscape right now 1 from survival to bureaucratic heroism in older stories the hero was a survivor with a shotgun in modern clifi the heroes are often scientists policy makers or community organizers the reading angle search for articles on anthropocene realism this is a movement that treats climate change as a normal part of life rather than a scifi shock key text the ministry for the future by kim stanley robinson it treats the creation of a carbon coin and international banking treaties as more exciting than any action scene showing that the real saving of the world happens in meeting rooms 2 solarpunk the antidystopia if cyberpunk is high tech low life solarpunk is high tech high hope this subgenre focuses on how humans can use technology solar biotech mycelium to live in harmony with a damaged planet the reading angle look for essays titled solarpunk narrates futures beyond climate despair they argue that we are tired of being told how we will fail we want to read about how we might actually succeed key concepts communities that practice radical recycling vertical forests in cities and decentralized energy grids 3 the end of the apocalypse literary critics are now writing about the apocalypse without apocalypse this is the idea that the world doesnt end with a bangit just becomes weirder and more difficult the reading angle search for articles on climate migration narratives instead of monsters or zombies the conflict comes from the ethical and social challenge of millions of people moving across borders due to rising seas key perspective many writers from the global south like amitav ghosh or cherie dimaline argue that for their cultures the end of the world already happened during colonization so their stories focus on resilience and the power of ancient knowledge rather than fear of a future disaster

today is the day to look forward not back a growing number of critics argue that the worldview centered on strict national borders is outdated in an era defined by global interdependence they point out that climate change economic instability pandemics and technological disruption do not stop at checkpoints or respect political boundaries according to this perspective leaders who continue to frame their policies around isolation nationalism or the idea of protecting our own are failing to recognize the realities of the modern world analysts say this approach reflects shortterm thinking and a reluctance to engage with the broader challenges facing humanity as a whole supporters of a more global outlook argue that true leadership requires acknowledging the interconnected nature of the planet they contend that focusing solely on national interests may win applause in the moment but ultimately positions a leader on the wrong side of history the criticism is blunt leaders who cling to old frameworks risk being remembered not as visionaries but as figures who lacked the foresight to adapt in this view legacy is not built by defending borders it is built by addressing global problems with global solutions observers note that the world is rapidly changing and the leaders who fail to evolve with it may find themselves defined by the limits of their own perspective rather than the impact of their actions

why greenland canada and the arctic are the new frontline we examine the geopolitical vulnerabilities emerging as climate change transforms the arctic from an impassable barrier into an accessible corridor we argue that western nations particularly canada and the united states face significant risks due to a lack of infrastructure and delayed modernization of defense systems like norad these gaps allow rivals like russia and china to exert influence through grayzone tactics such as sabotaging undersea cables or establishing de facto control over new shipping routes the analysis emphasizes that a weak northern posture invites strategic surprise and allows adversaries to set the rules for regional navigation and resource extraction ultimately the we advocate for urgent investment in domain awareness icebreaking capabilities and resilient communications to maintain sovereignty this comprehensive overview highlights how the melting ice cap has turned the high north into a critical front line for global security and maritime leverage

dermatology 101 seborrheic dermatitis why antidandruff treatments work until they dont if you deal with flakes redness or greasy scaling on the scalp eyebrows sides of the nose ears or beard area this probably sounds familiar you treat it it improves you stop it comes back seborrheic dermatitis isnt a hygiene issue its not because youre dirty and its not just dandruff its a chronic inflammatory condition driven by a threepart loop 1 an impaired skin barrier 2 malassezia yeast a normal skin organism that feeds on lipids 3 an overreactive immune response most people have malassezia on their skin that alone isnt the problem the issue starts when the skin barrier becomes compromised from harsh cleansers frequent washing actives stress illness climate or genetics when the barrier weakens water escapes transepidermal water loss lipid balance shifts malassezia byproducts penetrate deeper the immune system reacts aggressively that reaction causes redness flaking itching and scaling which further damages the barrier the loop feeds itself antifungals temporarily work ketoconazole selenium sulfide zinc pyrithione etc reduce yeast counts that often brings fast relief but theyre drying or irritating with repeated use which compromises the skin barrier so what happens yeast drops symptoms calm barrier weakens from repeated antifungal treatments treatment stops yeast rebounds inflammation returns this is why many people get stuck rotating antifungals indefinitely topical steroids suppress inflammation quickly they feel like relief but they 1thin the skin with repeated use compromising the barrier 2 can worsen rebound flares when stopped on the face especially this often leads to a cycle of dependence and recurrence seborrheic dermatitis responds poorly to force it responds better to stability that usually means 1 reducing stripping and overcleansing 2 using antifungals strategically and shortterm not constantly 3 simplifying routines and prioritizing barrier support this is where simple lowingredient occlusives including fats like tallow can help some people not by killing yeast but by slowing moisture loss restoring lipid balance creating a calmer skin environment less inflammation less immune overreaction less flare potential not a cure a stabilizer the same is true for mct oil mct oil is essentially refined coconut oil and for many people with seborrheic dermatitis myself included it can work extremely well the reason is simple malassezia yeast primarily feeds on longchain fatty acids especially lauric acid c12 true mct oil is refined to contain only mediumchain triglycerides typically c8 caprylic and c10 capric fats the yeast cannot metabolize when you apply mct oil youre effectively removing the yeasts food source and replacing it with something it cant digest yeast activity drops inflammatory byproducts drop and symptoms often improve quickly but mct oil doesnt fix the underlying problem a compromised skin barrier and an overreactive immune response so when mct oil is stopped seborrheic dermatitis usually returns often within days thats where barrier repair and lifestyle changes matter a simple beef tallow skincare routine can help rebuild the lipid barrier while lifestyle factors like diet sleep and exercise support immune regulation from the inside out spend any time on rsebderm and youll see the same pattern repeated people flare with junk food sugar alcohol fried foods and improve when they reduce them many also report fewer flares with consistent exercise and good sleep in other words theyre avoiding triggers and strengthening tolerance the goal isnt eradication its tolerance youre not trying to eliminate malassezia its everywhere youre trying to help your skin coexist with it again seborrheic dermatitis isnt a failure of cleanliness its a failure of balance restore the barrier avoid inflammation triggers and strengthen the immune system and many people find the cycle weakens instead of repeating if this kind of breakdown is useful thats what we focus on over at rtallowskincare barrier repair mechanismfirst explanations and what actually helps longterm lurkers welcome

flooding in his country in a message posted on facebook late sunday chapo said mozambique is facing a difficult moment he explained that saving lives and helping affected communities must come before international meetings he said the governments main focus is on rescue efforts safety and restoring damaged areas mozambique president daniel chapo addresses the nation as floods force him to cancel his davos trip to focus on rescue and relief efforts heavy rains cause widespread flooding heavy rains that began in mid december have caused major floods in several provinces the worst affected areas include gaza maputo and sofala provinces rivers in these regions have risen above danger levels increasing the risk of more flooding many roads homes and public facilities have been damaged some communities remain cut off due to destroyed bridges and flooded roads more than 400000 people affected according to the united nations office for the coordination of humanitarian affairs more than 400000 people have already been affected by the floods the un warned that the number could increase because rain is still falling in many areas families have lost homes crops and personal belongings many people are now staying in temporary shelters south africa sends rescue support neighbouring south africa has stepped in to help mozambique the south african air force has sent a helicopter to assist with search and rescue operations in flooded areas rescue teams are working to reach people trapped by rising waters and deliver food medicine and clean water floods also affect south africa heavy rains have not only affected mozambique parts of south africa have also experienced flooding especially in the northeast kruger national park one of south africas most famous tourist attractions was closed for several days because of floods on monday the park reopened to day visitors climate change worsens flood risk experts say flooding in southeastern africa has become more frequent and warn that such disasters may continue unless climate action and better disaster planning improve government focuses on emergency response president chapo has instructed government agencies to work closely with local leaders aid groups and international partners their goal is to rescue those in danger provide shelter and restore essential services such as water electricity and healthcare the us pulls out of 66 global organizations the us withdrew from 66 international organizations using antiwoke rhetoric to justify a move that strengthens its imperialist power details the united states has formally withdrawn from 66 international bodies stating that they no longer serve american interests the list includes the un framework convention on climate change unfccc un women unfpa un democracy fund unctad the peacebuilding commission and thematic cooperation bodies such as un water and un energy beyond un agencies the us has also withdrawn from key multilateral bodies addressing climate migration and governance including the intergovernmental panel on climate change ipcc and the international institute for democracy and electoral assistance idea us agencies have been instructed to end cooperation withdraw staff and terminate funding wherever legally possible removing american financial and technical support from development climate and governance programmes relied on heavily by dependent nations context trumps longstanding hostility toward multilateral institutions dates to his first term when he withdrew the us from the paris climate agreement unesco and the un human rights council cut funding to un peacekeeping and the who and repeatedly criticized the un as ineffective in his second term the administration has continued this course by cutting funding to additional un programmes declining to send a us delegation to major un climate meetings and publicly calling the un useless at its 80th anniversary while rejecting climate science trump has characterized international institutions as vehicles for global governance gender equality lgbtq rights and environmental regulation that conflict with us sovereignty and national goals framing these themes as part of a domestic antiwoke narrative the administration has increasingly violated international law including the blockade and strikes on venezuela strikes on iran without consulting the un and sanctions against the international criminal court after it issued warrants for israeli officials important to know the us withdrawal is part of a broader strategic trajectory in which washington is reshaping its engagement with the united nations and other multilateral institutions to prioritize its political and economic hegemony preparing for confrontation with its main imperialist rival china the antiwoke narratives also aim to indirectly strengthen farright parties in europe in order to bring the eu into greater dependence as with the league of nations international institutions such as the un are tools of imperialist power not independent arbiters of peace or world governance they exist to serve the interests of the most dominant states and when those interests conflict the organisations lose all effectiveness

the legacy of sncipt reviving assams ancient bark manuscripts through traditional wisdom and modern science in the verdant hills and riverine plains of assam a northeastern state of india known for its biodiversity and cultural richness lies a hidden treasure trove of knowledge etched on the bark of trees sncipt manuscripts crafted from the resilient bark of the snc tree aquilaria malaccensis have served as the medium for preserving assams literary religious historical and scientific heritage for over a millennium these handmade folios often adorned with vibrant pigments and sealed with natural varnishes represent a unique fusion of indigenous craftsmanship and environmental adaptation from the early medieval era to the early 20th century they chronicled everything from epic tales and devotional hymns to medical treatises and astronomical observations however as modernity encroaches and traditional practices fade many of these manuscripts are succumbing to the ravages of time humidity fungi and insects this article explores the intricate process of restoring and conserving sncipt manuscripts in ordinary rural settings where sophisticated museum technologies are unavailable by blending ancient assamese techniques with contemporary scientific insights we can ensure these cultural artifacts endure for generations the story of sncipt begins with the snc tree itself a species endemic to assam and prized not only for its bark but also for agarwood a fragrant resin used in perfumes and incense worldwide the tree thrives in the regions subtropical climate characterized by high rainfall and humidity levels that average 8090 during monsoons harvesting the bark requires careful selection of mature trees typically 2030 years old to avoid damaging the ecosystem once peeled the bark undergoes a meticulous preparation process passed down through generations it is dried under sunlight or smoke to remove moisture cut into rectangular folios measuring about 4060 cm in length and 1015 cm in width and then partially degummed using tutia copper sulfate pentahydrate cuso5ho this partial degumming is crucial it retains a portion of the lignin a complex organic polymer that binds cellulose fibers granting the folio exceptional tensile strengthup to 68 mpa in fresh samplesand resistance to tearing following degumming the surface is smoothed with tools like bamboo scrapers or stones and a primer of fatty pulse a paste made from boiled lentils or beans is applied to create a receptive base for pigments the hallmark of sncipt is its coating with hitl yellow orpiment ass and hengul cinnabar hgs natural minerals that serve multiple purposes they provide antifungal and insectrepellent properties add decorative borders in yellow and red hues and enhance the folios glossiness writings are inscribed using mah a herbal ink derived from fermented fruits leaves and ironrich compounds which bonds deeply with the lignocellulosic structure finally a lcoating made from lac resin dissolved in spirit is brushed on to seal the surface making it humidityresistant and increasing its lifespan to centuries under ideal conditions historically sncipt manuscripts flourished during the ahom and koch kingdoms particularly amid the vaishnavite renaissance led by saints like sankaradeva in the 15th16th centuries they documented the bhakti movements devotional literature such as the bhagavata purana and kirtan ghosa as well as secular works on elephant training hasti vidyarnava and astrology the earliest reference dates to the 7th century ce in banabhattas harshacharita describing sncipt as gifts from king bhaskaravarman of kamarupa ancient assam to king harshavardhana this exchange highlights assams role in cultural diplomacy across ancient india unlike palmleaf manuscripts tlapatra used in southern india or birchbark bhjapatra in the himalayas sncipt was tailored to assams wet climate where paper would quickly degrade today tens of thousands of these manuscripts survive but most are stored in rural satras vaishnavite monasteries or village homes far from climatecontrolled archives traditional conservation involved placing them on bamboo racks hendli above firewood kitchens for smoke exposure which repelled insects and absorbed moisture with the advent of lpg stoves this practice has declined leading to increased vulnerability some custodians still apply neem azadirachta indica extracts annually leveraging its azadirachtin content for pest control but this is sporadic and insufficient against persistent threats like fungal growth from aspergillus or termite infestations the degradation patterns are telling manuscripts without full hengulhitl coatings show brittleness discoloration and edge fraying due to lignin breakdown from humidity those exposed to water develop mold spots while insect damage manifests as holes and tunnels a poignant example is a 200yearold copy of adi dashama from 1868 ce preserved at bor alengi bogi ai satra in jorhat where pages have split along fibers another a 300yearold adikanda ramayana at cooch behar state library formerly part of assam reveals postcreation conservation hitl applied to margins and hengul to borders even over breaks indicating ancient repair techniques modern interventions using paper conservation chemicals have backfired isopropyl alcohol cetrimide thymol and ammoniastandard for paperreact adversely with sncipts ligninrich composition scientific experiments on centuryold folios immersed for two hours show drastic changes fourier transform infrared ftir spectroscopy reveals diminished peaks at 3428 cm oh in lignin and 2913 cm nh stretching indicating lignin dissolution xray diffraction xrd patterns display reduced cellulose crystallinity from 83 to as low as 13 with thymol signaling structural disorder scanning electron microscopy sem shows increased fibrous exposure with energy dispersive xray edx detecting losses in oxygen from 44 to 033 with isopropyl alcohol and copper from tutia mechanical tests via universal testing machine utm record tensile strength drops from 327 mpa to 264 mpa toughness from 026 mjm to 012 mjm and elongation at break from 1348 to 744 rendering folios brittle weight losses reach 85 in water and thymol attributed to leaching of hemicellulose and lignin confirmed by uvvisible absorbance above 230 nm mah ink however remains stable due to its hydrophilic bonding these findings underscore sncipts incompatibility with aqueous or alcoholic solvents which swell fibers and extract protective components given these risks a chemicalfree method inspired by traditional preparation is ideal for rural conservation it starts with mild physical cleaning using soft brushes or rubber erasers on blank areas to remove dust avoiding writings to prevent smudging for mending tears fresh sncipt from young bark is prepared via a streamlined processcleaning tutia degumming hotpressing for smoothnessand cut into patches adhesion uses bael gum from aegle marmelos fruits a polysaccharide blend 71 dgalactose 125 larabinose etc that dries clear and strong without staining next hengulhitl is applied to free spaces like margins leveraging their antimicrobial properties hitls arsenic sulfide inhibits fungal enzymes while henguls mercury sulfide deters insects through toxicity ground to 65 m particles and mixed with bael gum they match original colorspure hitl for yellow hengul for red or blends for aged tones this not only protects but restores aesthetic vibrancy increasing gloss from 1020 gu gloss units to 4050 gu the final step is lcoating lac resin heated in spirit applied thinly to seal against humidity it boosts tensile strength to 434 mpa and creates a hydrophobic barrier posttreatment manuscripts are sandwiched between hitlcoated wooden boards wrapped in red cotton cloth possibly for infrared reflection and stored in cool dry spots piloting on 14 glossiness rose by 200 and mechanical properties improved validating the methods feasibility in rural workshops using basic tools expanding on cultural significance sncipt embodies assams syncretic identity blending aryan austroasiatic and tibetoburman influences in satras like majulis auniati they are read during daily namghar sessions fostering community bonds conservation thus preserves not just objects but living traditions scientifically this approach offers broader lessons lignocelluloses durability inspires sustainable materials like biocomposites for packaging pigments natural biocides could inform green preservatives reducing reliance on synthetics challenges remain sustainable snc sourcing amid deforestation training rural artisans and digitization for access without common mistakes homeowners in kerala make when building their first house hi everyone i work with an architectural team in kerala thats been involved in residential construction and renovation projects for over 34 years over time weve noticed a few recurring mistakes that homeowners often make especially during their first home build i thought it might be helpful to share some of these here 1 underestimating the impact of the monsoon keralas climate is beautiful but tough on buildings many homes face water seepage damp walls and drainage issues simply because rainwater flow and site levels werent properly planned at the start 2 finalising the plan before understanding the budget a lot of people fall in love with a design and only later realise it doesnt match their actual budget this leads to compromises in materials or unfinished work having a realistic cost estimate before locking the plan can save a lot of stress 3 ignoring natural light and ventilation its easy to focus on room sizes and elevations but airflow and sunlight make a huge difference in comfort and longterm energy costs especially in humid regions like kerala 4 choosing materials without considering maintenance some finishes look great in the first year but dont age well in coastal or highhumidity areas thinking longterm can reduce maintenance costs and headaches 5 not planning for future needs many homes arent designed with expansion accessibility or changing family needs in mind a little foresight in layout and structure can make renovations much easier later ive seen how small decisions at the early stage can make a big difference in how a home performs over the years would love to hear from others here what was the biggest challenge you faced while building or renovating a house in kerala

lovable as you are regardless ill talk about different methods of hair removal lifestyle changes prescriptions home remedies so first ill talk about lifestyle changes for some diet exercise seems to daily reading article for varc practice nearly 26 million years ago northeastern ethiopia was home to more than one kind of early human relative offering a rare glimpse into the complex web of our evolutionary past researchers working at the fossilrich site of ledigeraru uncovered teeth that belonged to two very different lineages early members of the genus homo the group that would eventually give rise to modern humans and a species of australopithecus an apelike ancestor better known for walking upright but still retaining many primitive features this discovery is groundbreaking because it demonstrates with clear fossil evidence that multiple human species truly did live side by side challenging the oncepopular idea that evolution followed a straight stepbystep path from ape to human instead the picture is far more tangled with overlapping species evolutionary dead ends and surviving lineages that coexisted for long stretches of time the teeth themselves tell an important story the homo specimens dated to about 259 million years ago closely match other early human fossils found at the site including a 278millionyearold jawbone that is currently the earliest known evidence of our genus the australopithecus teeth dated to roughly 263 million years ago are slightly older but striking for another reason they do not belong to lucys species australopithecus afarensis which was once thought to have disappeared by this time instead they appear to represent another branch of the australopithecus family tree one that lingered longer than expected extending the timeline of this groups survival the implications are profound this overlap means that east africa around 25 to 26 million years ago was not home to just one or two species of hominin but at least four early homo australopithecus afarensis the newly identified australopithecus species from ledigeraru and another enigmatic species possibly related to paranthropus these groups may have occupied similar landscapes raising the possibility of competition for food and shelter or alternatively they may have specialized in different diets and behaviors that allowed them to coexist some might have shared water sources scavenging grounds or toolusing strategies while others could have stayed apart avoiding direct conflict even more intriguing is the timing the period between 26 and 25 million years ago was one of enormous change climates were shifting grasslands were expanding and some of the earliest known stone tools were beginning to appear in this dynamic environment the survival of some species and the disappearance of others may have been influenced by their ability to adapt to new challenges the ledigeraru fossils therefore dont just fill a gap in the fossil record they highlight a turning point in human evolution when multiple species were experimenting with survival strategies in the same landscape altogether the discovery offers one of the clearest windows yet into how messy diverse and experimental human evolution really was rather than a single line leading neatly to us the story is one of branches overlaps and unexpected survivors some of whom lived side by side with our ancestors before fading into extinction

green card approved in 4 months but not produced for 15 months after hi everyone ive relied on this thread to keep me sane throughout this process so i thought it was only fair to give back and hopefully help someone else my husband and i got married in april of 2025 i was on an f1 visa and he is a usc we had been together for 25 years at that point we decided to file without a lawyer because i was convinced i could complete a form correctly it turned out to be a lot of work and i learned a lot in the process so im happy we did it that way we started the process in june had our interview at the st paul field office in minnesota which is apparently one of the stricter offices according to this thread and it went well we are pretty young so we didnt have much to show in terms of life insurance policies etc what we didnt have were a brand new joint account and lots of pictures we live together in a place his parents own so we did not have a lease but we had the same address on our drivers licenses and all mail correspondences during our interview the agent mentioned that they really admired the document i submitted which outlined our story with lots of pictures of us over the years dating hanging out with friends and family and of course the wedding and milestones after that our entire interview was almost an hour long as the agent went through this document and asked us questions about it i noticed that the agent would purposely get facts wrong about our story to check if my husband and i would correct her rather than straight up asking questions otherwise our interview went really well and the agent even suggested a place for my husband and i to get lunch afterwards i was really scared going into this because of the political climate of the country the government shutdown happened during our timeline i never received any response on my ead due to policy changes and at the end my country was on the list of banned countries and i heard that others were being denied for that reason i feared getting detained at my interview because that was happening around the country our i130 and i485 were approved by the 3rd of december 2025 at this point i was able to start working while waiting for the delivery of my gc i read that it could take up to 3 weeks to get it after approval 30 days later my case status was still approved without any updates on my green card i called in to uscis to follow up and i was told that i would receive information on that in the next 3 weeks 2 weeks later my i485 was approved again and within 2 days of the second approval i received my gc in the mail my status on the uscis portal still says card produced so i highly suggest signing up for informed delivery with usps for free overall a very stressful time to be going through this process especially since this administration is unpredictable and unprecedented so we relied on fellow redditors experiences to navigate the unknown our timeline 06032025 i130 filed received by uscis receipt sent 07182025 sent i485 and i765 applications by mail 07212025 applications received by uscis 07222025 receipt notice sent by uscis priority notice date as 06032025 07242025 cheques cashed by uscis 07252025 biometric appointment date received and scheduled 08122025 08122025 biometrics appointment 08122025 initial request for evidence sent by uscis 08152025 initial request for evidence received immigration medical examination 09122025 evidence medical examination sent by mail 09172025 evidence received by uscis 09222025 interview date set 11032025 11032025 interview at uscis field office 11032025 status changes to case is being actively reviewed by uscis 11252025 i130 approved 11282025 rfe sent by uscis for i485 12012025 evidence sent to and received by uscis
